answers.explanation: Running Dijkstra over a full map costs more than a Bellman-Ford comparison per neighbor.
The failure is flooded to everyone in seconds, and every router recomputes.
Link state routers all share one map, so loops are prevented by design.
That's the point: every LSA reaches every router in the area.
P–Q–R–S: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. P–R–S costs 7, and P–Q–S costs 9.
Through Q costs 2 + 3 = 5, cheaper than the direct link at 6.
Q–R–S: 3 + 1 = 4, cheaper than the direct Q–S link at 7.
Small and simple is where distance vector shines: easy to configure, and the network is far below 15 hops.
Link state scales and converges fast. RIP would be slow and could hit the 15-hop limit.
